chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Wesley Helvey's Troubadors, full of Louisville band alumni
summary: Helvey's band had Jeff Cass, Milt Robinson, John L. Henderson, George Loving and drummer Charles Bloomer, all from the Louisville kid band, and paid better than Horace.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: How come he had an opening? That was fortunate, wasn't it?
Yeah, I guess so. Well, I think what happened, that he'd been playing around with a smaller band and he wanted to --

Yeah, he was bigger before, and I think he probably cut it down, and then he wanted to -- because when I got there, another one of the fellows out of the band was playing the trumpet. His name was Jeff Cass, and he had come out of Louisville, out of that band. We had played together, and he was on trumpet and I'm on a trumpet, and Milt Robinson's on trombone, so the whole brass section's out of there, you know.

Well, in the reed section was a guy named John L. Henderson. He was a good first, beautiful tone. He had been in that band. Another guy named George Loving played alto, he was out of the band also, out of the same band.
So there you got three bass and two of the reeds, and the drummer, this Charles Bloomer who I told you about. He was in that band. So we was right at home, you know.

So now we get in this band and we start travelling around again, and the guy is getting a little more work than Horace got, you know, than Horace Henderson did, and he's paying off, a little better businessman, you know. And it wasn't bad at all. So then we -- now we go back to Buffalo on a steady job, work a steady job then. I see some of the guys that I left there, like Russell and Luke that was with the band.
